bug.title: After a reload or fresh sign-in, an appellant's hidden post shows "Appeal" again instead of the filed appeal's state
bug.symptoms: sam appeals the hiding of his post; after a reload, and after signing in afresh, /discussion (and the paper page's Discussion tab) shows "Your post was hidden: ... Appeal" again instead of "Appeal filed on 18 Nov 2026 - panel not yet formed" The API is right: GET /v1/papers/{id}/threads with sam's token returns the post's appeal {status: "not_formed"}; with no token appeal is null The page fetches threads on the server without a token (initial data), and DiscussionTab never asks again once the browser knows the viewer is signed in ("only a retry asks again"), so every per-viewer field of the thread (own hidden records, appeal state) is missing
bug.expected: When the session resolves to a signed-in viewer (on mount, and whenever the viewer's DID changes, including sign-in and sign-out), the discussion tab re-reads the threads with the viewer's token and replaces the server-rendered anonymous data without flashing a spinner over content already shown; the hidden placeholder then shows "Appeal filed on {date} - {awaiting panel | panel not yet formed | decided: ...}" from the API on any device; tests cover an anonymous initial payload followed by a signed-in viewer whose payload carries an appeal
bug.actual: The appellant's filed appeal is invisible on the post after any reload
